Section cdc_child:005 (page 6) is the continuation of the COVID-19 vaccination notes, 'Special situations' for 'Persons who ARE moderately or severely immunocompromised.' No rules were produced.

Population: the 'immunocompromised' concept does not capture the 'moderately or severely' severity qualifier. That severity call is clinician judgment, and approximating it with the generic concept could misapply the schedule.
Age bands not represented: 'Age 6 months–4 years' has a lower bound in months, which cannot be expressed in whole-year ages. 'Age 5–11 years' and 'Age 12–17 years' are also not represented.

Dose counts depend on manufacturer and prior history. Unvaccinated persons need 4 doses (Moderna or Pfizer-BioNTech series) or, at 12–17 years, 3 doses (Novavax 2-dose series plus 1 dose). Incomplete series are completed with 1 or 2 further 2024–25 doses plus 1 dose 6 months later. Completed series of 3 or more doses get 2 doses of 2024–25 vaccine 6 months apart. Expected counts therefore depend on prior product and dose history, which a count-based immunization criterion cannot express without derivation.

Intervals not represented: 0, 3 or 4 weeks; at least 4 or 8 weeks after dose 2; 6 months later (minimum interval 2 months); dose 1 at least 8 weeks after the most recent dose; and the instruction to 'administer dose 1 4 weeks' or '3 weeks after most recent dose'.

Product rules not represented: 'Use vaccine from the same manufacturer for all doses'. Product eligibility varies by age band (Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech, and Novavax for 12–17 years). The covid19_vaccine concept does not distinguish manufacturer or 2024–25 formulation.
Optional additional doses ('May administer additional doses.*') are referenced to a footnote (*) that is not in this section. They are permissive, not a computable requirement.

The section is cut off mid-text ('COVID-19 vaccination - continued'). The 12–17 years 'Previous vaccination with Pfizer-BioNTech' and completed-series guidance continue on the next page and are not covered here.
